newsitem.title: UK: UK's Burton says to demerge Debenhams chain.
newsitem.headline: UK's Burton says to demerge Debenhams chain.

text.p: British retail group Burton Group Plc announced on Tuesday its intention to demerge its Debenhams unit, the household items chain and seek a separate stock market listing for it.
Burton said the demerger would "significantly enhance" shareholder value and was in the best interests of the group's shareholders and customers.
Burton said the remaining businesses, which include Top Shop, Principles and Dorothy Perkins would be reorganised into one single business, renamed and would retain its existing listing.
"This proposal would result in two strong independent companies each with a strong cash flow, in which Burton Group shareholders would participate," the company said.
Debenhams as a newly-listed department store company will have Peter Jarvis, former chief executive of Whitbread, as its chairman while Terry Green will be its chief executive.
The Burton Group also said its turnover for the 18 weeks for 18 weeks ending July 4, 1997 was up 9.7 percent. The turnover of Debenhams was up 14.2 percent.
